questions: Is the inversion number defined as the count of pairs (i, j) such that i < j and B_i > B_j, or i < j and B_i >= B_j?
Should the output for k = i-1 be printed on line i, meaning line 1 corresponds to k=0, line 2 to k=1, ..., line M to k=M-1?
Are the values of A_i and k guaranteed to be such that A_i + k does not overflow typical integer ranges, or should we compute modulo M directly to avoid overflow?
If M=1, is the output a single line with inversion number 0 (since all B_i are 0)?
Should the inversion count be computed modulo some large prime or other modulus, or output as a plain integer?
Is the sequence B defined as B_i = (A_i + k) mod M, where mod yields remainder in [0, M-1]?
For large N and M up to 2e5, is an O(N log N) solution expected, or are there performance constraints beyond time limits?
If multiple pairs have the same B value, do they count as inversions? (Depends on strict vs non-strict definition.)
